newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Tuesday, as the yen's firmer tone against the dollar triggered selling orders from local investors, traders said.
Prices were 160 to 310 yen lower, with the benchmark March 1998 contract down 200 yen at 16,070 yen per tonne.
Some months gained at the opening, reflecting the Chicago market's firm sentiment overnight, but the stronger yen triggered selling by the afternoon session, traders said.
Technical selling, following Monday's price gains, was also behind the weaker Tokyo market, they said. "Investors are now more interested in soybean contracts," a trader said.
The spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.09 per bushel at 0710 GMT, against $3.10-1/4 at Monday's close.
The spot March CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.12-1/4 at 0710 GMT, down from $8.21 from Monday's close.
